findings.assertion: The federal constitution's article 50(XXVIII) empowered Congress to choose a seat for supreme federal powers; the congressional decree of 18 November 1824 selected Mexico City. Choosing the capital was a legislative decision following debate over alternative sites, notably Querétaro.
findings.source_locator: McGowan document 1824.11.18.2, printed p.238 arts.1–2; Lozada León HTML lines 75–82
findings.limitations: Original 1824 decree imprint not viewed; later narrative conflates some voting events.

findings.assertion: The 1824 law described a circle centered on the Plaza Mayor with a two-legua radius, while article 3 required federal and State of Mexico experts to demarcate it. The law's geometrical description is not an independently verified boundary survey or modern GPS polygon.
findings.source_locator: McGowan documentary appendix 1824.11.18.2, printed p.238 arts.2–3
findings.limitations: Modern sources disagree on the number of meters per legua and on area; do not render exact map or accept 55 km² versus 220 km² uncritically.

findings.assertion: The 1824 decree placed the district's political and economic government under federal jurisdiction, provided an interim federally appointed governor, and continued existing municipal-election arrangements where consistent with the new law. The capital did not thereby lose every municipal council overnight.
findings.source_locator: McGowan appendix, printed pp.238–239, arts.4–7; Memoria Política lines 15–16
findings.limitations: Do not substitute 1928 abolition of municipalities for 1824's distinct administrative arrangement.

findings.assertion: At the November 18 1824 congressional sitting, separate commissions were assigned questions of State of Mexico compensation, political eligibility and rights of district residents, and district courts. Creation of a federal capital did not settle those jurisdictional questions in one act.
findings.source_locator: McGowan ed. documentary appendix 1824.11.18.1, printed pp.237–238; El Sol 20 Nov 1824 p.669 and Águila Mexicana no.220 cited there
findings.limitations: Contemporaneous newspaper issues are cited by the historian's transcription, not independently opened.

findings.assertion: The district was carved from the State of Mexico, prompting state authorities to relocate their capital; a 2013 edition of McGowan traces Texcoco (1827), San Agustín de las Cuevas/Tlalpan (1827–1830), and Toluca (1830). The federal district's institutional status later changed with 1836 centralism and the 1846–1847 federal restoration.
findings.source_locator: McGowan 2013, foreword printed pp.11–12 and analysis pp.45–46; Memoria Política lines 16–20
findings.limitations: The 1836/1847 timeline is a regime-level summary; exact implementing acts should be checked.

findings.assertion: The decree specifies the Plaza Mayor as the CENTER of the proposed district. A guide can have visitors look across today's Zócalo and explain that a legal jurisdiction was defined from this public space rather than by Mexico City's contemporary administrative perimeter.
findings.source_locator: McGowan appendix, printed p.238 art.2; contrast modern city layout only as interpretive prompt
findings.limitations: Do not claim a surviving 1824 boundary marker, physically measurable radius, or specific original survey origin point within plaza.

findings.assertion: The January 2, 1824 Ayuntamiento's descriptive register assigns named commissions for water and acequias, roads, markets, street lighting, paving, public hospitals, sanitation and schools. This documents the municipal government's everyday functions before the federal district decree.
geographies: Antiguo Palacio del Ayuntamiento / Plaza Mayor
findings.source_locator: Ibero Actas de Cabildo 1824 guide, cabildo 546 Jan 2, PDF p.2 (viewer index 1) visually checked
findings.limitations: This is a twentieth/twenty-first century index of minutes, not original handwritten cabildo folios; current building room mapping unverified.

findings.assertion: The descriptive index for the January 5, 1824 council session records an order to clear rubble from the Plaza Mayor and to put material on the San Cosme and Chapultepec causeways. The record connects Zócalo maintenance with movement of materials into peripheral infrastructure.
findings.source_locator: Ibero Actas de Cabildo year 1824, cabildo no.549 Jan 5, extract lines 98–108; page image for this entry not examined
findings.limitations: Do not assume material was moved as ordered; index summarizes an instruction, not completion accounts or surviving fabric.

findings.assertion: A peer-reviewed study identifies the 1843 demolition of the Parián market in the Plaza Mayor as a contested modernization project involving central authorities, Ayuntamiento and Mexican and Spanish merchants. The place can teach the difference between aesthetic redesign and economic displacement.
findings.source_locator: Lorenzo, Estudios de Historia Moderna y Contemporánea de México no.38 (2009), journal abstract
findings.limitations: Only abstract consulted; need full article, historic footprint, compensation case records and mapping before visitor field claims.

findings.assertion: The late-colonial 1782 division into eight cuarteles mayores and 32 menores continued as the background to early republican patrol and justice geography, according to Flores Flores's 2019 peer-reviewed research; court, watchmen and street lighting need separate archival identities rather than a generic 'police' institution.
findings.source_locator: Flores Flores 2019, published article abstract lines 45–51, map links in article page entries 35–44
findings.limitations: Abstract only; maps and patrol registers not directly examined; modern lines cannot yet be reconstructed.

findings.assertion: The 16 February 1854 decree redefined the Distrito de México through named places reaching San Cristóbal Ecatepec, Tlalnepantla, Coyoacán, Tlalpan, Xochimilco and the middle of Lake Texcoco; it also specified three external prefectures with seats in Tlalnepantla, Tacubaya and Tlalpan. Its territorial vocabulary was no longer merely the 1824 two-league circle.
findings.source_locator: McGowan edited document 1854.02.16, printed pp.250–251 arts.1–4
findings.limitations: Edited law transcription, not original gazette or an executed survey; do not portray later locations as within present CDMX without temporal layers.
